What proportion of insurance cost variance is attributable to modifiable lifestyle choices versus baseline demographic and socioeconomic risk factors? # MODIFIABLE LIFESTYLE: Find relationships between insurance cost and bmi, smoker, alcohol_freq, exercise_frequency, sleep_hours, stress_level # BASELINE DEMOGRAPHIC AND SOCIOECONOMIC FACTORS: Find relationships between insurance cost and age, sex, education, income, marital_status, household_size

insurance <- read.csv("data/medical_insurance.csv")
names(insurance)

#Making average annual premiumn based on smoke status
insurance |>
  filter(smoker == "Never") |>
  summarize(avg_no_smoke_prem = mean(annual_premium, na.rm = TRUE))
  avg_no_smoke_prem
1          589.2447
insurance |>
  filter(smoker == "Current") |>
  summarize(avg_curr_smoke_prem = mean(annual_premium, na.rm = TRUE))
  avg_curr_smoke_prem
1            801.2571
insurance |>
  filter(smoker == "Former") |>
  summarize(avg_form_smoke_prem = mean(annual_premium, na.rm = TRUE))
  avg_form_smoke_prem
1            641.5419
insurance <- insurance |>
  mutate(log_annual_premium = log(annual_premium))
#Ran anova test, next step is to do step down tests
summary(aov(annual_premium ~ smoker, data=insurance))
